title: Self-averaging of replica overlaps in the random field Edwards-Anderson model
abstract: The self-averaging of the replica overlap is proven in the Edwards-Anderson (EA) model under random field almost everywhere in the coupling constant space in any dimension. The EA order parameter is represented in terms of the derivative of the free energy density with respect to the random field strength, regardless of boundary conditions. Tasaki's correlation inequality for finite-dimensional spin glass models shows that the expectation of the squared replica overlap is bounded by the squared EA order parameter. These simple evaluations enable us to prove that the variance of the replica overlap vanishes in the infinite-volume limit. The self-averaging of the replica bond overlap is proven also in the EA model with Gaussian exchange interaction without random field. Short-range spin glass models have been shown to behave differently from mean-field spin glass models with RSB phase.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that the replica overlap in the random field Edwards-Anderson spin glass model exhibits self-averaging in the infinite volume limit. This is achieved by relating order parameters to derivatives of the free energy density and employing sophisticated mathematical inequalities. The result confirms a specific behavior for finite-dimensional disordered systems, distinguishing them from mean-field models.
main_problem: The central problem is proving the self-averaging of the replica overlap in the Edwards-Anderson (EA) spin glass model when subjected to a random external field.
main_result: The variance of the replica overlap is proven to vanish in the infinite-volume limit for almost all coupling constants, establishing self-averaging properties for this disordered system.
method: The proof utilizes advanced techniques involving derivatives of the free energy density with respect to the random field strength and relies on correlation inequalities (like Tasaki's) to bound the variance terms.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Edwards-Anderson (EA) spin glass model, defined by a Hamiltonian incorporating quenched random couplings ($J_{x,y}$) and an external random magnetic field ($h_g$). The analysis is performed in the thermodynamic limit (infinite volume).
key_observables: Replica overlap ($R_{\alpha, eta}^L$), Edwards-Anderson (EA) order parameter ($q_{EA}$), and the free energy density ($\varphi_L$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), random field strength ($h_g$), system dimension ($d$), and the infinite volume limit ($L 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The proof requires that the free energy density be independent of boundary conditions for the random field EA model, and it is restricted to short-range interactions.

paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by relating order parameters to derivatives of the free energy density, proving self-averaging theorems using correlation inequalities, and contrasting these findings with mean-field models like SK.
why_interesting: While focused on classical spin glasses, the mathematical techniques used for analyzing quenched disorder and replica symmetry breaking are foundational tools in modern statistical physics that can inform theories of quantum disordered systems or complex energy landscapes relevant to AMO physics.
